title: 'Best Targets Tonight' ranks purely by transit altitude, so it recommends obscure galaxies that transit in daylight and pass through the zenith
reasoning: The claimed module exists and is wired. packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/planning/tonight_ranking.dart derives the darkness window from TwilightTimes with the described astronomical->nautical->civil->sunset degradation (null under midnight sun), drops anything with hoursAboveMinAlt <= 0 inside that window, and ranks the survivors with TargetScoringService.scoreTargetForNight over [window.start, window.end] at minAltitude 30. mosaic_targets.dart:186 calls it through compute(), and BOTH consumer surfaces (desktop tonight_tab.dart and mobile mobile_widgets/search_sheet.dart) read the same provider, so there is no unfixed second copy. tonight_tab.dart:311-397 does headline hoursInDarkness + peakTime and carries the exact subtitle and tooltip quoted. One inaccuracy in the summary, not in the code: it says 'No new weighting was invented', but rankTonightTargets blends a NEW _catalogQualityScore (magnitude / size-vs-FOV / type) at 30% against the night score at 70% (tonight_ranking.dart:203), so the panel's order can differ from the planner's pure TargetScoringService order that the summary claims parity with. The blend pushes toward brighter, well-framed objects, i.e. WITH the finding ('obscure galaxies') rather than against it, and is itself test-covered, so I read this as a summary overstatement rather than a defect.
evidence: Severance: replaced the body of _rankTonightTargetsOffThread with the pre-fix key (calculateObjectVisibility, keep transitAltitude > 30, sort desc on transitAltitude, take 20). tonight_ranking_provider_wiring_test.dart went 3/3 RED - 'refuses a daylight culmination' returned DECOY-ZENITH instead of REAL-TARGET, 'every target the card offers has dark hours and a dark peak' failed with peakTime outside the window, and the FOV test returned SMALL where LARGE was expected. mosaic_targets.dart restored byte-identical (diff clean); test/planning + tonight_night_window_test.dart back to 30/30 green. Also checked _currentNightDateProvider (catalog_astronomy.dart:153) truncates observationTime to a night DATE, so the ~6.4s isolate job cannot be re-triggered every minute.

title: Search hint badge reads '⌘K' on Linux and Windows, where the shortcut is Ctrl+K
reasoning: packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/utils/platform_shortcuts.dart exists with shortcutModifierLabel()/shortcutLabel(key) switching on defaultTargetPlatform exactly as described, is exported from skotiq_ui.dart:25, and both claimed call sites use it (search_header.dart:670 and redesign/command_bar.dart:198). A repo-wide grep for the literal Command glyph and for the \u2318 escape across packages/ and apps/ finds ZERO remaining occurrences in production Dart - only doc comments and test expectations - so no third badge was missed. Checked the widened label cannot overflow: the command-bar entry is a fixed 200px Row whose 'Search' label is the Expanded child, so 'Ctrl+K' (~35px at fontSize10) takes its intrinsic width out of ~112px of slack; the header badge is an InputDecoration suffixIcon that sizes to content.
evidence: Severance: replaced shortcutLabel('K') in command_bar.dart:198 with a hardcoded '\u2318K'. skotiq_app test/screens/planetarium went 148 green -> 145 pass / 3 RED, all three in search_command_focus_test.dart, which locates the command-bar Search control via find.text(shortcutLabel('K')). The other site is covered independently by search_shortcut_badge_platform_test.dart, which pumps SearchHeader under debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride for linux/windows/macOS and asserts the glyph is absent on the first two. command_bar.dart restored byte-identical (diff clean); re-ran 148 green. skotiq_ui full suite after the barrel export: 263 green.

title: Object search has no exact-designation path: typing a catalogue number returns 175 fuzzy matches
repairSummary: Test-coverage repair only, no behaviour change. The fix has TWO production call sites - the star loop at object_search.dart:416-429 and the DSO loop at 583-590 - and only the DSO one was covered: deleting the star branch entirely left all five shipped tests green. Added 'a padded star catalogue id is an exact designation too' to packages/skotiq_planetarium/test/search_designation_ranking_test.dart, using a HYG-shaped star with zero-padded ids ('HIP 005300') against a DSO whose common name merely starts with the query, so the star can only win through the designation path. It goes red (returns NGC9999) when that branch is deleted. dart format run.
reasoning: _splitDesignation, _isExactDesignation, _exactDesignationScore = -1 and _bareNumberCatalogs = {m, ngc, ic} all exist as described, and the designation check is applied in both search loops (star loop short-circuits with `continue`; DSO loop applies last and unconditionally so it overrides every fuzzier band). I checked the narrowing claims against the REAL data rather than the summary: running the regex mentally over packages/skotiq_planetarium/assets/opengnc/NGC.csv, the only non-alphanumeric OpenNGC names are the ' NEDnn' component suffixes, which _splitDesignation correctly refuses (letters after digits), and composite ids like 'ESO 287-052' and '2MASX J...' are refused as claimed. The prefix pin is real: a non-empty query prefix must match the designation's prefix exactly, so 'UGC 6720' cannot answer NGC6720, and a bare number is gated to M/NGC/IC so it cannot promote HD 6720. One scope caveat stated for honesty: the fix is ranking-only, so the finding's literal symptom ('returns 175 fuzzy matches') is unchanged - the result LIST is the same length, only its head is now deterministic. The summary is upfront about that ('Added designation-aware ranking'), and the operator-visible failure (a lucky-by-brightness first result and a wrong Enter/fly-to) is genuinely cured, so this is not a relocation.
evidence: Severance A (DSO loop): deleted the designationQuery block at object_search.dart:583-590; search_designation_ranking_test.dart + search_resolver_test.dart went 13 green -> 4 RED. Severance B (star loop): deleted the block at 416-429; ALL tests stayed green - that is the gap I repaired. After adding the new test, severance B fails with 'Expected: HD006720 / Actual: NGC9999'. object_search.dart restored byte-identical (diff -q clean) after each experiment. Full skotiq_planetarium suite afterwards: 502 passed, 1 failed (see regressionsFound - not attributable to this shard).

title: Region detail opens on a viewport-filling empty preview with no empty state; everything informative is below the fold
reasoning: Both cause fixes are present and load-bearing. region_detail_screen.dart:220-243 replaces the free AspectRatio with a LayoutBuilder sizing the hero to math.min(constraints.maxWidth * 2/3, _kCutoutMaxHeight = 320) inside a SizedBox, with BoxFit.cover on the cutout; _EmptyCutout (lines 311-348) renders 'Nothing imaged here yet' plus the next-step sentence inside the preview instead of a bare glyph. The growth-card change is CONFINED to the caller: atlas_growth_curve.dart swaps AdaptiveChartContainer.fixed(height: 170) for ConstrainedBox(minHeight: 170) at that one placeholder; the shared analytics/widgets/adaptive_chart_container.dart is untouched in git status, so no other screen's chart geometry moved. Checked for the usual missed-fourth-surface: the only other AtlasRegionCutout preview is atlas_region_card.dart:45, a 16:9 hero inside a grid cell whose width is already bounded, so it never had this defect. The claimed pre-fix magnitude checks out numerically - severing the cap put the coordinate line at dy 1126 on a 1600x900 window, consistent with a ~1035px hero (1552 * 2/3).
evidence: Severance A (hero cap): removed the math.min so the hero is free again; region_detail_empty_state_test.dart failed with 'Expected: a value less than <430> / Actual: <1126.33>'. Severance B (growth card): restored AdaptiveChartContainer.fixed(height: 170); BOTH tests failed with real RenderFlex overflows - 14px on the 1600x900 pane and 51px at 360dp - which independently corroborates the summary's claim that a fixed 170px box clips EmptyState.compact. Both files restored byte-identical (diff clean); skotiq_app test/screens/your_sky back to 36 green. I also ADDED (not a repair - the shipped test already caught severance B) 'the empty region detail lays out at 360dp without overflow' to region_detail_empty_state_test.dart, which pumps the whole screen at phone width, asserts the 320px cap does NOT bind there (preview height < 320, i.e. the phone keeps its 3:2 proportions), and scrolls to the growth placeholder so an overflow anywhere in the column fails the test. dart format run.
